seo.title: Borgobianco Resort & Spa: Puglia Honeymoon Review (2026)
seo.description: Modern Pugliese resort near Polignano. Score 78/100, from $450/night. Verdict, suite pick, 7-night itinerary.

content.verdict: Borgobianco is the modern, accessible alternative to the famous Savelletri masserias — a 38-room resort built in 2008 on a 15-acre olive estate 5 km inland from Polignano a Mare on the Adriatic coast, designed in a contemporary white-washed Pugliese vernacular that nods to the masseria tradition without faking 18th-century stone. The position is the genuine selling point: a 6-minute drive to Polignano a Mare (the cliff town with the Grotta Palazzese cave restaurant), 25 minutes from Bari airport (the closest international gateway for honeymooners flying in from London or Frankfurt), and 30 minutes from Alberobello and the trulli. The amenity offer is full: a large outdoor saltwater pool, a heated indoor pool, the 1,200 sqm B-Spa with a thalasso circuit, hammam, and 8 treatment rooms (the operation is genuinely credible — the spa was the first in Italy to be certified by the Italian Thalassotherapy Association after San Domenico), tennis, a kids’ club, and the Due Cortili restaurant under chef Stefano Veneziani serving creative Pugliese cooking on the courtyard terrace. The honeymoon move is one of the new Suite Borgo with private rooftop terrace, or a Junior Suite Olivella with garden. The defining moment: dinner at Grotta Palazzese in Polignano (the famous sea-cave restaurant, 10 minutes away) as a half-day excursion from the masseria, then back for an aperitivo in the gardens. Caveats: the contemporary architecture lacks the genuine 16th-century historical feel of San Domenico, Torre Maizza or Borgo Egnazia — for purist masseria fans this is the immediate disqualifier; the immediate setting is more “Pugliese countryside” than dramatic; and service is excellent at four-and-a-half-star level rather than the choreographed five-star of the Rocco Forte property. But for honeymooners flying into Bari, wanting a serious spa, and prioritising Polignano-a-Mare access over the dense Itria Valley masseria cluster, Borgobianco is the obvious pick and at substantially lower rates than its more famous neighbours 30 km south.
content.best_room: A Suite Borgo with private rooftop terrace — the most contemporary and private rooms in the resort. For the more traditional option, a Junior Suite Olivella with garden access. Avoid the standard Camera Trifora rooms — lovely but smaller and without the private outdoor space.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Arrival and Due Cortili dinner
itinerary_7_nights.description: Drive 25 minutes from Bari. Check-in to your Suite Borgo, welcome Spumante. Aperitivo in the gardens. Dinner at Due Cortili.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Polignano a Mare day
itinerary_7_nights.description: Drive 6 minutes to Polignano. Morning wandering the cliff town. Lunch at Grotta Palazzese (the sea-cave restaurant) at noon. Afternoon swim at Cala Porto. Return for the spa.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Itria white towns
itinerary_7_nights.description: Driver-and-guide to Alberobello, Locorotondo, Cisternino. Lunch at a Cisternino fornello. Return for the pool and dinner at the masseria.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Thalasso and Monopoli
itinerary_7_nights.description: Morning at the B-Spa thalasso circuit. Lunch at the masseria. Afternoon drive to Monopoli (15 min) for the old town. Dinner at Due Cortili.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Slow masseria day
itinerary_7_nights.description: Long breakfast on your terrace. Cooking class for orecchiette. Lunch with your pasta. Afternoon massage. Quiet dinner.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Bari and northern Puglia
itinerary_7_nights.description: Drive to Bari (25 min) for the old town and the Castello Svevo. Lunch in the Bari Vecchia. Afternoon at the Adriatic. Final dinner at Due Cortili.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Slow departure
itinerary_7_nights.description: Final breakfast. Drive to Bari for departure.

caveats: Contemporary build, not a real 18th-century masseria. Choose San Domenico or Torre Maizza for historic.
Service is excellent at 4.5-star level — not the choreographed Rocco Forte 5-star.
Setting is Pugliese countryside, not dramatic. The property is the destination, not the location.

faqs.question: Good for honeymooners?
faqs.answer: Excellent value for couples flying into Bari, wanting full spa-and-pool amenity, and prioritising Polignano access. Less atmospheric than the Savelletri masserias.

faqs.question: Best time to visit?
faqs.answer: May, June, September. October still good. Open most of the year (limited operations December–February).

faqs.question: Book in advance?
faqs.answer: Suite Borgo and Junior Suite Olivella 4–6 months for May–September. August requires 9 months.

faqs.question: Adults-only?
faqs.answer: No — Borgobianco has a kids’ club and welcomes families. Expect families in summer school holidays.

faqs.question: Best room type?
faqs.answer: Suite Borgo with private rooftop terrace. Junior Suite Olivella for the garden alternative.

faqs.question: How to get there?
faqs.answer: Bari (BRI) 25 minutes by car — the closest airport. Brindisi (BDS) 90 minutes. Hire car at BRI or hotel transfer €100.
